newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-CHANCE FOR AJAX TO SALVAGE SOMETHING.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CHANCE FOR AJAX TO SALVAGE SOMETHING.

text.p: Ajax Amsterdam's European Cup quarter final first leg clash with Atletico Madrid on Wednesday offers them a chance to salvage glory from what has been their most miserable season in years.

Out of the domestic cup competition and trailing Dutch league leaders PSV Eindhoven by 18 points, last year's beaten finalists will be hoping to rekindle sparks of the form which swept them to consecutive European Cup finals in 1995 and 1996.
Ajax coach Louis van Gaal, who leaves the team at the end of the season to be replaced by Denmark's Morten Olsen, has struggled to motivate a team hit by injuries and personnel changes.
To make matters worse a potentially unsettling spat erupted between Van Gaal and Winston Bogarde over the utility player's refusal to accept a place on the bench for Wednesday's match.
An angry Bogarde was pictured by Dutch television storming away from the Arena stadium on Monday night after Van Gaal sent him home from training.
Atletico also seem out of the hunt for the Spanish league title, lying in fifth position 13 points behind leaders Real Madrid, and are primed for their biggest game of the season.

For Ajax, Van Gaal is expected to field the same side that recently trounced arch rivals Feyenoord 3-0, raising hopes that the team has ridden out its injuries and is ready to take the second half of the season by the scruff of the neck.

Key Ajax strikers Patrick Kluivert and Jari Litmanen, who both scored against second-placed Feyenoord, will be up against an Atletico defence chosen by coach Radomir Antic which helped the Madrid team to a league and cup double last season.
Up front, Antic is expected to try a completely new formation by moving midfielder Jose Luis Caminero into the forward line to take the place of suspended fellow Spanish international Kiko Narvaez.
Caminero scored twice in Saturday's 3-2 league win over Sevilla, before being hit by a stomach bug scare.
Another surprise is the probable inclusion of midfielder Carlos Aguilera, who has hardly started a game since returning to Madrid from Tenerife in the close season.

Aguilera will be responsible for controlling the right side of midfield, up against the pacy and deceptive Marc Overmars, while Argentine captain Diego Simeone will face elusive Nigerian international winger Tijani Babangida on the left.

Set-piece specialist Milinko Pantic will be working as link-man with an attack aiming to prise open an experienced Ajax back line of Mario Melchiot, Danny Blind, Richard Wittsche and Frank de Boer for precious away goals.
The Dutch team could have an advantage in their relatively light schedule since the winter break, with last Sunday's game against Sparta of Rotterdam postponed.

A lacklustre second half to the season and an unconvincing home performance against Atletico Madrid could leave the Amsterdammers with the prospect of missing out on European competition for the first time since the early 1990s when they were barred for a year after a missile throwing incident.

Ajax - goalkeeper: Edwin van der Sar; defenders: Mario Melchiot, Danny Blind, Richard Witschge, Frank de Boer; midfielders: Ronald de Boer, Jari Litmanen, Kiki Musampa; strikers: Tijani Babangida, Patrick Kluivert, Marc Overmars.
Kluivert, Melchiot and Babangida all have one yellow card.

Atletico Madrid - goalkeeper: Jose Molina defenders: Delfi Geli, Santi Denia, Roberto Solozabal, Toni Munoz; midfielders: Radek Bejbl, Carlos Aguilera, Milinko Pantic, Diego Simeone; strikers: Jose Luis Caminero, Juan Eduardo Esnaider.
